sections.html:
New Lenox is a village in central Will County, about 36 miles southwest of downtown Chicago. Population is 28,893 (July 1, 2025 estimate). Owners live in 92.4% of homes, the middle home value is $399,900, and households average 3.05 people, so these are mostly family-sized houses.

Much of the village grew from the 1990s onward. The census count rose from 9,627 in 1990 to 17,771 in 2000 and 24,394 in 2010, so houses from those years are common. Commutes average 32.7 minutes, which is why the Metra station and the I-80 and I-355 ramps are the first things a commuting buyer looks up.

sections.h2: Village permits and open permit work
sections.html:
Most construction and homeowner projects need a village permit, including sheds, decks, pools, fences, roofs, lawn irrigation, siding, window replacement, room additions and basement remodels. Homeowners may do the work themselves, but any contractor must be registered with the Village before the permit is issued.

  • The minimum building permit fee is $75.00. Fees for garages, remodeling, room additions and in-ground pools depend on project cost.
  • Small jobs such as fences, sheds, driveways, roofs and windows can be reviewed over the counter and issued the same day if the application is accurate. Larger reviews can take up to two weeks.
  • Online applications are accepted for furnaces, water heaters, air conditioners, demolition, driveways, electrical upgrades, fences, generators, irrigation systems, roofs, rooftop solar, sewer repairs, and window, door and siding replacement.
  • Online applicants should hear a status within two business days, and no work may begin until the permit is paid for and issued.

Private sidewalks, concrete or paver patios, dog runs and playhouses under 100 square feet do not need one. Community Development answers questions at 815-462-6490, and Village Hall takes in-person applications from 8:30 am to 5 pm on weekdays.

If a permit was never closed out, the Village's inspection steps apply. It asks for 48 hours of notice for building inspections and 24 hours for water meter and plumbing inspections, and it charges a fee for a failed inspection, including one where the work is not ready when the inspector arrives.

Winter adds a second limit. From December 1 through March 30 the Village prohibits placing concrete flatwork, and it regulates timing and insulation for footings and foundations. Bonds are accepted in place of exterior concrete during those months. If you have an unfinished driveway apron or public walk, ask the Building Department how the bond works before a closing date is set.

The Village also keeps a Vacant Property Registration form on its permits page. If the house will sit empty during a sale, ask Community Development whether that registration applies to you.

sections.h2: Recording a deed with Will County
sections.html:
New Lenox deeds record with the Will County Recorder of Deeds at 158 N. Scott Street in Joliet, phone 815-740-4637. The fee schedule effective October 1, 2025 lists $90.00 for a standard document and $118.00 for a non-standard one, and the $19.00 Rental Housing Support Program surcharge is part of those totals.

The recorder's deed checklist asks for:

  • The preparer's name and mailing address, and a return address for the document.
  • The permanent index number and a legal description.
  • A notarized original deed, not a copy.
  • The grantee name and address, and the name and address for tax bills.
  • A completed transfer declaration or exemption under the Illinois transfer tax law.

The checklist also names nine municipalities whose transfer stamps must be on a deed: Aurora, Bolingbrook, Channahon, Joliet, Naperville, Park Forest, Romeoville, University Park and Woodridge. New Lenox is not one of them. Ask Village Hall whether any local stamp or payoff step applies to your closing.

New Lenox School District 122 runs the elementary and middle schools. High schoolers attend Lincoln-Way Community High School District, which serves New Lenox, Frankfort, Mokena, Manhattan and a small part of Tinley Park. Lincoln-Way Central and Lincoln-Way West are in New Lenox, and Providence Catholic High School is also in the village.

U.S. Route 30 is the main east-west road, with Cedar, Gougar and Nelson roads running north and south. I-80 and I-355 both pass through. The Metra Rock Island District station is at U.S. 30 and Cedar Road, and a second station at Laraway Road is on the SouthWest Service line.

January averages about 21 degrees Fahrenheit and July averages 73, with 137 days a year at or below freezing. Those swings are hard on roofs, gutters, driveways and basement sump systems. Keep receipts for roof work and the sump pump, since both come up in nearly every sale.

The New Lenox Community Park District maintains 40 parks and athletic fields on nearly 600 acres. The 22-mile Old Plank Road Trail passes through the village, and Hickory Creek State Nature Preserve and Hadley Valley Preserve add more trail miles. A house near the trail or a park is worth a line in the listing.

A sale here goes in a straight line. Start by checking permits for any deck, roof, finished basement or addition, and call Community Development at 815-462-6490 if a record is missing. Next, settle the contract terms, including whether the buyer takes the house in its present condition and who handles any unfinished exterior concrete.

Then prepare the deed to the recorder's checklist: original notarized signature, legal description, permanent index number, and the transfer declaration or exemption. Ask Village Hall whether any payoff or final billing step applies. A cash buyer can usually work to your date and skip the repair negotiation, which helps a seller with unpermitted work or a roof near the end of its life.

Keep your closing statement and the recorded deed together afterward. If a permit question comes up later, those papers show what was done and when.

sections.h2: What to have on hand for the buyer's review
sections.html:
Buyers and their inspectors tend to ask the same few questions about a house here. Have answers ready for the roof, the sump pump, the furnace and any deck, shed or finished basement. For each, a permit number or a contractor receipt is the best proof. If something was done without a permit, say so plainly and let the buyer decide how to handle it, or sell to a cash buyer who takes the house as it stands.

Also gather your most recent water bill, the parcel number and your loan payoff details. Having them in one folder shortens the time between accepting an offer and setting a closing date.

faqs.q: Do I need a village permit before selling my New Lenox house?
faqs.a: Not to sell, but open permits and unpermitted work can come up in a buyer's review. The Village requires permits for most construction projects, so call Community Development at 815-462-6490 if you remodeled, added a deck or replaced a roof.

faqs.q: Which office records a New Lenox deed?
faqs.a: The Will County Recorder of Deeds in Joliet. The standard document fee is $90.00 since October 1, 2025, and the deed must be an original with a notarized signature, a legal description and a permanent index number.

faqs.q: Does New Lenox charge a municipal transfer tax stamp?
faqs.a: The Will County deed checklist names nine municipalities that issue transfer stamps, and New Lenox is not among them. Ask Community Development at 815-462-6490 before closing to confirm.

faqs.q: Can I sell a New Lenox house with unfinished concrete work?
faqs.a: Yes, but winter timing matters. The Village bars concrete flatwork from December 1 through March 30 and accepts a bond in place of exterior concrete during that period, so ask the Building Department what the bond requires.

faqs.q: How old are most New Lenox houses?
faqs.a: Most of the building came between 1990 and 2010. The count rose from 9,627 in 1990 to 17,771 in 2000 and 24,394 in 2010, so houses from those years are common.
